extracted.intended_audience: PR and marketing professionals / communicators pitching broadcast media
extracted.subtask_short: creating effective B-roll for broadcast PR
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for PR teams on planning, shooting and supplying B-roll footage that helps secure and enhance broadcast news coverage. Focuses on what makes B-roll useful to broadcasters and how to balance quality, quantity, relevance and reusability under newsroom/time constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: B-roll purpose: add context, depth and transitions
rubrics_metrics.description: B-roll is short clips of footage added into a story to add context. It helps to demonstrate the PR story through cutaways from A-roll, fill gaps and set the scene, and is a great way to make smooth transitions between shots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use B-roll to enhance the principal shots — it acts in the same way images do to a news story and can add intrigue to interviews by setting the scene and providing depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include concrete, story-relevant illustrative cutaways
rubrics_metrics.description: B-roll should demonstrate the PR story through cutaways from A-roll and include footage that directly illustrates what the story is about.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from the page: demonstrations (e.g., RNLI lifeguards demonstrating Float), animals being fed or checked at a sanctuary, shots that directly relate to the interview content so the B-roll adds narrative value and intrigue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types/variety of effective B-roll shots
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended shot types to use as B-roll to ‘add colour’ and set the scene.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples listed: pans of the location; interviewees entering and leaving the area; drone footage; employees working at a desk or in the background; time lapse of the crew setting up the shot. Include a variety to allow smooth transitions and visual interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide owned / copyright-free footage when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: If sourced outside of the broadcaster, B-roll is often copyright and cost-free to make your footage and story more appealing than other stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplying your own high-quality, licensable (or free-to-broadcast) footage increases the likelihood that broadcasters will use your story because it reduces legal/cost barriers and editing overhead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make footage reusable for follow-ups and other stories
rubrics_metrics.description: B-roll is not redundant after its use in one story; it is useful in follow-up media pieces, other relevant stories, or stories in the same location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture shots that can be repurposed across multiple segments or future coverage to maximise the value of your shoot — ‘a good bit of B-roll can be the making of many broadcast PR stories.’

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance quality and quantity — collect enough high-standard B-roll
rubrics_metrics.description: You’ll need to strike a balance between getting quality B-roll and enough of it while remembering it doesn’t make up the content; it provides context, padding out the narrative of a story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although B-roll is often shot under time pressures, collect sufficient footage of a high standard so it’s worth using and improves the overall story. Do not rely on B-roll to substitute for strong A-roll/content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliver ready-to-use, well-curated footage to make the media’s life easy
rubrics_metrics.description: PR is about making the media’s life as easy as possible — if you can hand them a perfectly shot piece of footage with a great B-roll they can pop on the news agenda and not have to spend any time editing, you’re onto a winner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to supply footage that requires minimal editing and is broadcast-ready; well-curated clips increase the chances of immediate pickup by busy newsrooms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritise timeliness and excitement to meet newsroom needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsrooms have smaller departments, tighter budgets and deadlines, but demand strong, recent and exciting video content; B-roll can provide a fresh and exciting perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture recent, newsworthy, and visually engaging material that will perform well both on TV and on social media to help brands fight for airtime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan shoots to succeed under resource and time constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: B-roll is often shot under time pressures and with stretched resources; you should still aim to collect decent footage that is high standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare shot lists (including the recommended shot types), prioritise must-have illustrative shots, and work efficiently on location so that limited time still yields usable, compelling B-roll.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make B-roll compelling to increase chances of coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: A good bit of B-roll can be the making of many broadcast PR stories — compelling footage can make a good story great and help clinch coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on visually interesting, relevant moments (demonstrations, candid action, location atmosphere) that will stand out to producers and editors reviewing many pitches.
